basic needs (food, shelter) for El Paso County nonprofits (the one-third general-charity share)

In 2024 about $737,500 went to three diocesan Catholic-school channels (Houston, San Antonio, El Paso) for tuition aid. Eligibility is limited to the dioceses of Galveston-Houston, San Antonio and El Paso, so a Diocese of Austin school cannot apply.
funder_intel.giving_trend: Burkitt Foundation grants to El Paso Community Foundation: $921,000 (2021), $1,017,100 (2022), $1,205,983 (2023), $1,326,253 (2024): rising. The 2025 Form 990 reports $1,444,791 to the El Paso Community Foundation as non-cash assistance with no cash grant (Schedule I, TY2025, filed August 2026), which may be an asset transfer. Total assets: $34.98M at the end of 2023.
funder_intel.outlook: The 2025 filing reports a $1.44M non-cash transfer into the El Paso Community Foundation, and the program is now listed as the 'Burkitt Foundation Perpetual Fund'. Together these suggest the money may be moving into a permanent fund at the community foundation, but neither source says so. The El Paso Community Foundation page lists an application window of July 1 to August 1 and no other changes.

Texas example: the Diocese of Fort Worth uses it for tuition assistance at a Fort Worth Catholic school (2019). A diocesan flyer (Fort Worth, Feb 2024, seen only as a search excerpt) says each school gets a grant every year but that low collections have 'significantly decreased the grant awards per school'.

The 2026 collection materials ('Building Our Mission to the Missions') announce no program changes. A Texas school benefits only through its diocese's application, and only for African American or Native American students and ministries.

grants.grant_name: CorWorks Parish Innovation Grants (OSV Institute for Catholic Innovation)

Parent organization (Our Sunday Visitor, Inc.) 2024 Schedule I: 24 grants over $5,000 totaling $835,211; parish and school grants $5,000-$26,700; the largest went to its home diocese ($312,404) and the USCCB ($178,500).
funded_focus: parish teams turning charitable outreach into sustained community impact (design thinking, prototyping, community listening)
evangelization and Catholic innovation projects
heavy concentration in OSV's home region (Fort Wayne-South Bend, Indiana) in 2024 grants

No CorWorks grant recipients have been published yet: the program is new, and a 'second cohort in 2026' is mentioned without naming the first cohort's parishes.
funder_intel.giving_trend: Our Sunday Visitor, Inc. grants to organizations (Form 990): $2,407,967 (2021), $2,082,485 (2022), $1,880,242 (2023), $915,205 (2024): falling steadily, down by half in 2024. CorWorks seed grants were too new to show up in these filings.

The diocese page (fetched 2026-10-15) describes a 2026 second cohort: applications May 25 - July 24, 2026, accelerator week August 17-21, 2026, and a roadmap through November 2026. The main page says applications are open, with a window of 'Oct. 9 - Nov. 20' and the next cohort starting January 2027. Up to six parishes per diocese can join at once, at no cost to the diocese. Seed funding is described as a 'possibility', not guaranteed.

The school official must attend the district's consultation meetings, supply the data the district asks for, sign the Affirmation of Consultation, and help plan services. Services, not cash: the district stays the fiscal agent, hires/oversees staff and keeps title to materials and equipment, and all services must be secular, neutral and non-ideological. If the district does not consult meaningfully, the school may complain to the TEA private nonprofit school ombudsman. The private school takes part through the district's consultation; there is no grant application to submit.

grants.description: Ecumenical grants for year-long projects that renew public worship and connect it with intergenerational faith formation and discipleship. Parishes and religious schools are named as eligible, and past grantees include Catholic projects.
grants.geography: United States and Canada
grants.eligibility_notes: Christian worshiping communities with tax-exempt status (congregations and parishes; seminaries, colleges and religious schools; hospitals and others). Team needs support of the pastor or key administrator. No grants to individuals, building renovations or construction; equipment capped at 10% and staff compensation at 20% of the grant.
focus_areas: Preaching, baptism and the Lord's Supper
Universal design and cultural engagement in worship

past_awards.purpose: baptism formation for parishioners and families of the newly baptized
synodal listening to reconnect young adults to worship and faith formation
liturgy and musicianship formation for Spanish-speaking parish musicians
liturgical dance and sacred arts workshops

funder_intel.award_levels: Worshiping Communities grants are $8,000-$25,000 (program page). Individual amounts are not published.
funded_focus: liturgy and sacraments formation
preaching
intergenerational and youth worship engagement
worship music and the arts
hospitality and community connection through worship
funder_intel.catholic_school_track_record: Catholic parishes and dioceses win grants every year (2024, 2025 and 2026 examples above). No Catholic K-12 school grantees were found; religious schools are eligible but the program funds worship projects, not academics.
funder_intel.giving_trend: Worshiping Communities grants by grant year (CICW recipients database): 40 (2022), 62 (2023), 142 (2024), 128 (2025), 66 so far in 2026 (June round). The June 30, 2026 round made 77 grants (66 worshiping communities and 11 teacher-scholars). More than 1,500 grants since 2000.
funder_intel.outlook: Announced June 30, 2026: the program now runs twice a year. The next deadline is October 15, 2026, for projects starting January 15, 2027. The institute has an interim director, and Lilly Endowment funding continues.

grants.description: Awards to K-12 educators for innovative classroom projects that improve student learning, either existing projects or ones they want to launch. Award checks are payable jointly to the educator and the school and must be used for the project.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Full-time educators, teachers, principals, paraprofessionals or classified staff employed by an accredited K-12 public OR private school in the US; awards are made without regard to creed or religion. funder_intel.catholic_school_track_record: Not found. Private school educators are eligible ('an accredited K-12 public or private school'), but no Catholic school winners were found in the sources checked.
funder_intel.giving_trend: 100 winners in 2019 (Hays Free Press, Nov. 2019). 50 winners a year under the current rules. More than $6 million awarded since the program began. Smaller than in 2019.
funder_intel.outlook: The 2026 cycle closed April 30, 2026 (extended from April 17). Finalists are notified in August, top three are chosen over the summer, and payments are made by December. No program changes announced.

grants.grant_name: WeTeach_CS Preferred Provider Workshops (free summer CS, AI and cybersecurity PD for Texas teachers)
grants.funder: WeTeach_CS, Texas Advanced Computing Center, The University of Texas at Austin
grants.deadline_notes: 2027 workshops must run between June 7 and July 23, 2027; WeTeach_CS picks its providers by December 18, 2026 and then posts each workshop's page and application. In 2026, applications were reviewed on a rolling basis until spots filled (one AI workshop asked for applications by May 29, 2026).
grants.amount: Free PD of at least four days, plus stipends, travel help and/or classroom materials (2026 stipends ran from $80 a day up to $700, with travel reimbursement of up to $1,000 at one workshop)
grants.typical_award: $400 - $700 stipend (2026 workshops)
grants.description: WeTeach_CS pays curriculum providers to run free summer workshops, at least four days long, for Texas teachers in computational thinking, computer science, cybersecurity and AI. Participants get stipends, travel help and/or classroom kits. 2026 examples included ethical generative AI and data science with MIT App Inventor (grades 6-12) and a middle school machine-learning workshop with micro:bit kits. This is paid training with materials, not a school grant.
grants.geography: Texas (workshop sites vary; providers serving rural or underserved regions get priority)
grants.eligibility_notes: Texas educators. Each workshop sets its own grade band and priorities; for example, the 2026 App Inventor AI workshop was for Texas educators teaching grades 6-12 with priority to Title I schools, and some workshops were limited to one ESC region. No public-school-only rule was found.

WeTeach_CS reports it has reached 469 schools in 251 districts since 2015 (Nov. 2022) and more than 600 K-12 educators.
funder_intel.giving_trend: Summer 2026: 33 workshop listings from about 26 providers. funder_intel.outlook: Summer 2027 provider applications open October 13 - December 1, 2026 (selections December 18, 2026); the 2027 call selects up to 12 providers (about 26 appeared in 2026; the 2026 cap was not stated), with workshops between June 7 and July 23, 2027. WeTeach_CS also flags 2027 scholarships, mini-grants, Change Maker Awards and a 2-day 2027 Summit.

Over $4 million to more than 100 nonprofits since 2004. Competition: more than 214 applications across the Women's Fund and Hispanic Impact Fund in 2024 (45% of winners first-time partners); 125 applications vetted in 2025 (31% first-time).
